title: Run
description: One execution of one benchmark binary, written whether it succeeded or failed. A Run describes itself: it holds the parameters the binary was given, the provider's own words for where it ran, the bytes that ran, and the box's environment before and after. Nothing in it is a judgement. Every value of the form sha256:<hex> names a blob stored at blobs/sha256/<hex> whose bytes hash to it. The root is closed: a key not listed here makes a record invalid.

id.description: A version 7 UUID, minted on the box when the binary is launched.

boot.description: The kernel's boot id. The Runs of one boot share it.

started_at.description: Read just before the binary was launched.

ended_at.description: Read just after the binary exited.

benchmark.description: The benchmark's directory name under benchmarks/.

params.description: Exactly the parameters delivered to the binary, as LM_PARAM_<KEY>.

samples.description: Delivered to the binary as LM_SAMPLES.

source_commit.description: The git commit the source archive was made from.

source.description: The source archive the box unpacked and built from.

build.description: The name of the build, as given to the benchmark's Makefile.

compiler.description: The compiler's own first line of version output.

command.description: What the build printed: the commands it ran.

resolved_flags.description: What the compiler resolved its flags to on this box, such as -march=native.

provider.description: The provider's own words for where this ran, verbatim. `name` says whose words they are; the other keys are that provider's.

environment.description: The box's environment dump taken just before the launch and just after the exit. Each names an index blob that lists the dump's sections by hash.

runner.description: The runner that launched the binary: a blob listing every file of runner/ with its hash.

exit.description: How the process ended: its exit code, or the signal that killed it. `timeout_seconds` is present when the runner killed it for running that long.

events.description: Every line the binary printed to stdout, parsed, in order (schemas/events.schema.json). Parsing stops at the first line that is not a JSON object; `stdout` always holds the lines as printed.

events_error.description: Present when a stdout line could not be parsed: the line's number and why.
